relations.subject: Li Fang-Kuei
relations.evidence: His alma mater Tsinghua University began to publish his complete works in 2005.

relations.subject: Li Fang-Kuei
relations.evidence: He earned a BA in linguistics at the University of Michigan in 1926 after only two years of study.

relations.subject: Li Fang-Kuei
relations.evidence: He then did graduate study under Edward Sapir at the University of Chicago, where he was Sapir's first graduate student. From Sapir he learned phonetics, field methods, and American Indian languages.

relations.subject: Li Fang-Kuei
relations.evidence: Li was also a student of Leonard Bloomfield at this time, from whom Li learned Germanic linguistics and textual analysis.

relations.subject: Li Fang-Kuei
relations.evidence: Li also studied Indo-European linguistics, especially Greek and Latin, from Carl Darling Buck at Chicago

relations.subject: Li Fang-Kuei
relations.evidence: He received an MA in 1927 and a PhD in 1928. His dissertation Mattole: An Athabaskan Language was published in 1930.

relations.subject: Li Fang-Kuei
relations.evidence: in 1928 Buck secured a 6-month fellowship at Harvard University for him, where he studied Sanskrit and Tibetan.

relations.subject: Li Fang-Kuei
relations.object: Institute of History and Philology of the Academia Sinica
relations.evidence: in 1929 he returned to China and, along with Y. R. Chao and Luo Changpei, became a researcher at the Institute of History and Philology (歷史語言研究所; Lìshǐ yǔyán yánjiūsuǒ) of the Academia Sinica then located at Beijing.

relations.subject: Li Fang-Kuei
relations.evidence: Li taught Chinese language and linguistics at Yale University from 1938 to 1939

relations.subject: Li Fang-Kuei
relations.evidence: after World War II taught at Harvard University from 1946 to 1948.

relations.subject: Li Fang-Kuei
relations.evidence: During the same period he was working on a dictionary at the Harvard–Yenching Institute

relations.subject: Li Fang-Kuei
relations.evidence: followed by another year teaching at Yale from 1948 to 1949, where his students included Nicholas Bodman.

relations.subject: Li Fang-Kuei
relations.evidence: In 1949, he became professor of Chinese at the University of Washington, where he taught from 1949 to 1969

relations.subject: Li Fang-Kuei
relations.evidence: after which he taught at the University of Hawaiʻi until his retirement in 1974.

relations.subject: Li Fang-Kuei
relations.evidence: He also worked at Academia Sinica, now in Taiwan, in 1973.
